# Jimmy Essex

**Jimmy Essex** (born November 18, 1984) is a British actor, dancer, and musician. He is best known for his role as Adam Donovan in the Channel 4 soap opera *Hollyoaks*, which he played from 2016 to 2018. Prior to his acting career, Essex was a member of the music group MITSOTU, which reached the Judges' Houses stage of *The X Factor* in 2012. His other credits include the Netflix fantasy series *The Sandman* and the stage play *GHBoy*.

## Early life and education
Essex was born in London, England, and grew up in the Harrow area . He trained in performing arts at the Urdang Academy in London .

## Career

### Music and dance
Essex began his career in the music industry as a dancer and singer. He worked as a backing dancer for high-profile artists, including Janet Jackson and The Saturdays .

In 2011, Essex formed the "urban pop" group MITSOTU (an acronym for *Music Is The Soul Of The Universe*) alongside James Collins and Holly Cooper . The trio, who met at college, performed at various schools and events to build a following . In 2012, the group auditioned for the ninth series of the ITV reality music competition *The X Factor* . They were mentored by Louis Walsh in the "Groups" category and advanced to the Judges' Houses stage of the competition but were eliminated before the live shows .

### Television and film
In 2016, Essex was cast in the Channel 4 soap opera *Hollyoaks* as Adam Donovan . He was introduced alongside actors Maxim Baldry and Luke Jerdy, who played his brothers Liam and Jesse, respectively . The character was established as a hairdresser and a half-brother to the established character Grace Black .

Essex's storylines on *Hollyoaks* included romantic entanglements with Maxine Minniver and Darcy Wilde, as well as complex family dynamics involving his father, Glenn Donovan . Essex departed the series in 2018 after two years in the role . His character was written out in a dramatic exit storyline in which Adam was shot and killed by his father, Glenn, after it was revealed Adam had been working as a police informant against him . Essex expressed satisfaction with the conclusion of his character's arc, describing the exit as "shocking" and effective for the show's narrative .

Following his departure from *Hollyoaks*, Essex appeared in the 2022 Netflix series *The Sandman*, based on the comic book by Neil Gaiman. He portrayed the character Carrion in the episodes "Collectors" and "Lost Hearts" . His film credits include the role of Peter in the horror film *A Dark Path* (2023) and Felix in the short film *Daddy Issues* (2024) .

### Theatre
In late 2020, Essex made his professional stage debut in the play *GHBoy* at the Charing Cross Theatre in London . Written by Paul Harvard, the production explored themes of chemsex, trauma, and mental health within the gay community in East London . Essex played the lead role of Robert, a man dealing with grief following the death of his father while navigating addiction and relationships .

## Personal life
Essex is openly gay . He has been in a relationship with musician Charles Simmons since 2013 . The couple announced their engagement in January 2019, following a proposal by Simmons during a holiday in Sri Lanka .

Countdown to the Christmas celebration in Harrow town centre
------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 1](https://i2-prod.mylondon.news/article6326882.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200f/TM140002Adam-Courtney.jpg)

X Factor stars MITSOTU: James Collins, Holly Cooper and Jimmy Essex

Today we can reveal that X-Factor 2012 stars MITSOTU - who are from Harrow and Pinner - will be performing at the Harrow town centre lights switch on.

The event, on Saturday, November 30, on is one of the highlights in the borough’s calendar and this year promises to be an exciting afternoon.

There will be street performers, a sneak preview of this year’s Harrow Arts Centre pantomime, performances from Dhol Drummers and the Harrow Steel Pan Orchestra, as well as appearances from Bob the Builder and Peppa Pig and a spectacular fireworks display.

Harrow Community Radio will be hosting proceedings and there will be lots of opportunities for shopping for presents at the Christmas market in St Ann’s Road.

It is in Harrow town centre on Saturday, November 30, from noon to 6pm.

The Observer has teamed up with Harrow Council to run the Christmas Card competition and are inviting children from all over the borough to send in a colourful design to be in with a chance of winning the fabulous prize – switching on Harrow’s Christmas lights.

We have received lots of sparkling, creative entries already – so a BIG thank you to all the schools and families who have already taken part. The deadline for entries is on Monday, November 25 – so there is still time to get involved.

Harrow Council leader Councillor Susan Hall said: “This exciting competition will give a lucky child the chance to be at the centre of our Christmas celebrations. It is also a great opportunity to show your creative flair so if you haven’t sent your entry in then make sure you do so, for your chance to be part of the fun.”

HOW TO ENTER

Get your creative thinking cap on and come up with a festive Christmas Card design.

It could include Father Christmas and his reindeer, a snow-covered winter scene in your area, a snapshot of your favourite things at Christmas, or perhaps what you imagine the Christmas lights will look like in Harrow town centre.

Send your design (no larger than A4) together with your name, age, address, and signature from a parent or guardian by Monday, November 25, 2013, to: Christmas Card Competition, Harrow Observer, Gazette House, 28 Bakers Road, Uxbridge, UB8 1RG.

Terms and conditions

All entrants must be under the age of 16 and have permission from a parent/guardian to enter.

The winner will be selected by a panel of judges.

The winning child’s parent/guardian must be happy for their child’s picture to be taken for the newspaper and council communications related to the competition.

The editor’s decision is final and usual TMS terms and conditions apply.

New gay play GHBoy aims high but is only a partial success – review
===================================================================

By [Chris Selman](https://www.gaytimes.com/author/chris-selman/)

10th December 2020

![Image 1](https://www.gaytimes.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/GHBoy2-590x370.jpg)

**The new play, written by Paul Harvard and directed by Jon Pashley, has opened at London’s Charing Cross Theatre.**

For those looking for a feel-good festive show, GHBoy is not the one – set in East London’s party scene, it explores issues of drug addiction, sex addiction, and their impact on mental health. There’s also talk of an unnamed killer following the unexplained deaths of several young men. At times it’s a difficult watch. The story focuses on the life of Robert (Jimmy Essex), a gay man in his 30s, who has led a pretty hedonistic lifestyle up until the present day. He tries to get himself clean and back on the straight and narrow after his much-younger boyfriend Sergi (Marc Bosch) unexpectedly proposes.

There are a few issues. There’s a problem with pacing – the first few scenes feel like a very slow burn, and it takes a long time to find its feet and introduce us to something interesting. We also weren’t sold on several of the elements of the story; the main topics explored here are ones we’ve seen on the stage countless times before. Gay men taking drugs, going to clubs, going to saunas, struggling to get clean – we’ve seen it before, and in more creative and engaging ways.

When GHBoy does start to consider something a bit more novel, it shies away before we get a proper look. The narrative about the mysterious killer is touched upon a few times but feels disappointingly unresolved by the play’s conclusion. Potentially interesting discussions surrounding the shame associated with an HIV+ diagnosis, or the fetishisation of black men within the gay community, are only touched upon superficially before the conversation is swiftly moved on. Given that both of these issues are clearly integral to the life of the main character, we’d have liked to have seen more in-depth and considered explorations of these.

![Image 2](https://www.gaytimes.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/GHBoy.jpg)

The show is redeemed by a handful of impressive performances. Jimmy Essex, as protagonist Rob, is on-stage the whole time in what appears to be a physically demanding role. We particularly enjoyed Aryana Ramkhalawon as best-friend Jasminder and Buffy Davis as Rob’s mum Debbie – both brought some warmth and a sprinkling of much-needed humour to proceedings. Sadly we received a post-press night update that Buffy Davis will not be completing the run due to injury – she will be replaced by Nicola Sloane for the remaining performances.

At times GHBoy feels like it’s biting off more than it can chew – weighing in at 80-minutes, it’s trying to cover a lot of issues, many of them pretty big and serious, in a very short time frame – and unfortunately it’s only a partial success. It aims high but never quite gets there – we left the theatre wanting a lot more.

**GAY TIMES gives GHBoy – 2/5**

_More information can be found [here](https://charingcrosstheatre.co.uk/theatre/ghboy)._

An “urban pop” band of best friends who liken themselves to Rihanna are just two shows away from securing a life-changing performance at The O2.

MITSOTU – which stands for Music is the Soul of the Universe – have made it through to the regional finals of the UK’s largest national music competition for original acts, Live and Unsigned.

With around 40,000 musicians entering across the country, the trio of singers will join 60 acts in the Hayes regional live shows battling to make it through to the area finals.

Holly Cooper, 22, from Petts Wood makes up a third of the band.

She said: “There were about 2,000 people on the day we auditioned just in our region.

“It was amazing because we’ve been doing it in front of our friends and families but this was different and we were quite nervous.

“We’re all best friends and we met at college when we were 16.

“We love to do pop and more commercial things – it’s been great.

“We want to get signed and release amazing music and inspire children.”

This year the annual competition is giving the best acts opportunities to play at some of the country’s biggest festivals including Beach Break Live and Strawberry Fields.

New to 2012, Live and Unsigned is also being filmed for a Sky TV fly-on-the-wall documentary.

![Image 6: News Shopper: Urban pop band MITSOTU reach the brink of success](https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/leisure/entertainment/9541521.urban-pop-group-mitsotu-sail-through-live-and-unsigned-auditions/)

If MITSOTU triumph in the area finals, they will be performing at London’s biggest indoor festival in July, Live Fest at The O2, before celebrity judges including former Slade front man Noddy Holder and Radio 1’s Annie Nightingale.

Holly added: “This competition is great because it’s for original artists and we sing all our own stuff – it’s not like the X Factor where you have to sing other people’s songs.

“We are like urban pop – like Rihanna but a band.”

James Collins, 22, and Jimmy Essex, also 22, make up the rest of the group.

Since they got together around a year ago, MITSOTU have been travelling around local schools to play for youngsters and inspire them to chase their dreams.

Recently, the trio visited Cooper’s Technology College in Chislehurst and Bishop Justus C of E School in Bromley.

“We perform three songs and give an inspirational speech.” Holly said.

“The response has been amazing – as a kid you want to be star and we tell them you actually can do it if you set your mind to it.

“We tell them they have to work hard to get somewhere and when we leave they are really inspired.

“It’s really rewarding doing what we love and helping others at the same time.”

Acts are competing for the main prizes which include £10,000 to be spent on development, a £10,000 publicity investment, gigs at festivals in Canada, Italy and Latvia, a UK tour of up to 100 shows and a UK festival tour including guaranteed slots at Norfolk Spectacular, Boardmasters, London Summer Jam and Lancaster Music Festival.

* * *

MITSOTU will next perform in their regional finals on Sunday March 11 at the Beck Theatre in Grange Road, Hayes.

Tickets are £8.

‌  

MITSOTU, an urban three-piece featuring 21-year-old James Collins, from Macfarlane Road, narrowly missed out on a place in the talent show’s live finals having made it through to the ‘judges’ houses’ stage of the competition.

‌  

But, despite a strong audition, James and bandmates Holly Cooper and Jimmy Essex, lost out to rival group MK1 for the final live slot.

Adam Donovan, played by Jimmy Essex, was seen being brutally murdered on Tuesday night's first-look Hollyoaks.

‌  

The character was shot by his own father Glenn on the E4 episode, following a shock showdown in the woods.

‌  

Glenn, played by Bob Cryer, discovered that Adam had been working undercover with the police to bring him and his criminal gang down.

As they came face to face it seemed as if Adam was going to pull the trigger on his dad but he decided to walk away.

![Image 3](https://i2-prod.ok.co.uk/article14289646.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/1152386_hollyoaks_glenn_de210a955bb9d5ac959736bbb4b26e16)

UK Theatre Newsletter Get all the top news & discounts for UK & beyond. ✨ Sign Up We chatted to Jimmy about entering the theatre industry in a pandemic, the misconceptions of gay culture that the show addresses and why he loves playing challenging roles. **Can you explain the story of _GHBoy_, and the role of Robert, who you're playing?** The story is centred around Robert and his addiction to chemsex and cheating. It's about his discovery of himself, finding out who he is and coming to terms with something really terrible that happened to him and the major effect it's had on his life. **How are you feeling about making your West End debut?** Amazing, and it's been the most incredible experience so far. Coming into something so new and exciting in itself feels like such an achievement. It's something very different to anything I've ever done and I just love the challenge of it. I couldn't be happier really. **Does it feel odd to be making your debut during a pandemic?** Yeah, of course. But the good thing is, I have nothing to compare it to! I didn't know how it was going to work; to an extent, you're making the rules as you go along because nobody's faced this before, so we're just figuring things out as we go. There have been a few growing pains, but I think we're there now. We get how it has to work and how we can do it safely; it's been challenging, but also really exciting. **What drew you to go from your TV work to the theatre?** I love theatre, and theatre is what got me into acting anyway. I think as a medium, it's incredible; there's something so magical about it. I also wanted to push myself, and I love this role of Robert. I think the role really spoke to me; there's something about his journey of discovering himself that really scratched an itch for me, so I just jumped at the chance. ![Image 37: Interview: Jimmy Essex Talks GHBOY at Charing Cross Theatre Image](https://cloudimages2.broadwayworld.com/upload13/2076432/Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch-Marc-Bosch-Sergi-Castell_-Credit-Adam-Stevens-Productions-768x432.jpg?format=auto&width=1400) Jimmy Essex & Marc Bosch in _GHBoy_ **How are rehearsals going?** Great! They've been going really well. We're obviously having to do social distancing, we're getting tested quite regularly and we have to wear masks for some of it too. So it's all been learning how to adapt to this crazy new world we're living in. But it's been great - the cast is wonderful and the director, Jon Pashley is amazing. I know Paul Harvard, who wrote the play, from years and years ago, so it's been nice to reconnect with him as well. **It's Paul Harvard's debut play - is it nice to star in someone's debut work as your West End debut?** Yeah, definitely. I think because it's new and it's his first play, everyone wants to make it as amazing as it can be, just out of the love for it and because we want to make it special for everyone. Plus, we're the first people doing it, so there's something really exciting about that. We're paving the way for it, which is lovely. **The show tackles misconceptions around gay culture and promiscuity - why is this such an important message?** I think there are taboos and a hushness around a lot of gay culture; not just from the heterosexual community to the gay community, but also within the gay community too. There are a lot of misconceptions and stigma that come with certain lifestyles and choices. So, I think it's really good to put a human face on this subject and make it relatable. I just think it's really important to shine a light on it. **The show has a very diverse cast with a range of ages and experiences, both on stage and behind the scenes. That must be a great team to be part of.** Yeah, definitely. I think we all feel very blessed. Not only because we're trying to do something that seems impossible, but also because of the range of people involved and the experiences they're bringing to the project. I think it says so much about what we want the message to be; it's about acceptance of everyone. ![Image 38: Interview: Jimmy Essex Talks GHBOY at Charing Cross Theatre Image](https://cloudimages2.broadwayworld.com/upload13/2076432/Sylvester-Akinrolabu-Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch_-Credit-Adam-Stevens-Productions.jpg?format=auto&width=1400) Jimmy Essex and Sylvester Akinrolabu in _GHBoy_ **It's been a really weird year. How have you been coping during the pandemic?** To be honest, at first, I loved it. Once I focused on just getting back to basics, appreciating what I have and the people I have around me, as well as the magic and the enjoyment in everyday life, there was something really special about that. I loved it. Then about halfway through, I was pulling my hair out. I'm quite an active person and I love to be doing things, and so it's been quite a struggle. I think the one good thing I took from it was the fact I was with my partner the whole time and we got to actually spend some time together, which is a rarity. And also, just finding enjoyment; my garden has never looked so good! **You're about to make your debut, but what would your dream theatre role be in the future?** Any kind of theatre that inspires some kind of conversation, and a role that is as challenging as Robert in _GHBoy_. I think those are the things that I look forward to, and as I'm growing in my career, are things that make me question myself and normatives that I may have already created in my own brain. Those juicy roles where it changes not only the audience, but my perspective of things, that's what appeals to me the most. **Why should people come and see _GHBoy_?** We're putting on this amazing show, so come and support theatre! I think it will surprise people too. I think people have a misconception about what the play is going to be about and how they're going to feel about it. I think they'll walk out with a completely new mindset, having gone on this amazing journey with this guy. I think there's something really, really special about that. _GHBoy at Charing Cross Theatre [from 3 December](http://ticketsareavailablenow/)_ _Photo credit: Adam Stevens_ ### NEXT UP [FOR A SHEPHERD'S Bush musician hopes his band will 'go global' after making the finals of a major talent competition.

‌  

James Collins, 21, who grew up in and still lives in Macfarlane Road, formed MITSOTU with friends Holly Cooper and Jimmy Essex, both 22, just over a year ago.

‌  

The trio, who met at college, already have successful careers as performers, with James having just returned from a tour with Janet Jackson and Jimmy from a tour with The Saturdays, while Holly has been a contestant on X Factor.

‌  

But they decided to try their hand as a group after impressing observers with their urban pop sound and entered Live and Unsigned, one of the country's major talent competitions for original musicians.

After waltzing through the auditions, they are now preparing for the regional heats before, they hope, an appearance in the grand final.

‌  

James likens the group's style to that of Rihanna and hopes they can become Britain's biggest urban pop band.

"It's really exciting," said James, who grew up with his grandmother. "The judges seemed to really like us and we are hoping to make it big and become known around the world.

"We have all got music and performing in our blood and it is our dream to inspire people and get them to think 'If they can do it, so can we'."

Article continues below

The winners of the competition are judged the country's biggest unsigned act and could win prizes including £10,000 for publicity and slots at music festivals.

Live and Unsigned's Chris Grayson said: "Live and Unsigned is all about originality, live ability and credibility. We don't accept demos and everyone auditions live."

Hollyoaks star Jimmy Essex is officially engaged to boyfriend of six years
==========================================================================

"So... This happened."

By [Chris Edwards](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/628110/chris-edwards/ "Chris Edwards")Published: 21 January 2019

_[Hollyoaks](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/)_ star Jimmy Essex has revealed that he is officially engaged to his boyfriend of six years, musician Charles.

The actor, who played Adam Donovan on the soap, took to Instagram earlier today (January 21) to confirm the news to his followers.

Jimmy shared a picture of himself and his (now) fiancé sharing a kiss while holding up the engagement ring.

What to Read Next
-----------------

![Image 5: instagram](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/instagram.f282b14.svg?primary=currentColor&id=link-out-embed)[View full post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/Bs5vzYalYOM/)

While Jimmy hasn't made a habit of discussing details of his relationship in public, this isn't the first time he's declared his love for his boyfriend on social media.

In 2017 he shared a [tribute to his partner](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a835296/hollyoaks-jimmy-essex-celebrates-his-fourth-anniversary-boyfriend/) as they celebrated their fourth anniversary.

![Image 6: instagram](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/instagram.f282b14.svg?primary=currentColor&id=link-out-embed)[View full post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/BXm6_VIB7m6/)

"Thank you for putting up with me, 4 years!!" he captioned the post. "You must be mental! I love you."

Earlier that year, the pair re-enacted one of the best scenes from _Enchanted_, [sharing a picture of them manning a boat](https://www.instagram.com/p/BUm2nKPhpFe/?taken-by=jimmy_essex) in New York City's Central Park, and he also shared another photo of the two of them along with a message.

"Never a dull moment with this one!!!" he wrote. "Thank you for making me sooooOooo happy!!"

![Image 7: instagram](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/instagram.f282b14.svg?primary=currentColor&id=link-out-embed)[View full post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/BWXNVAbBxzZ/)

Jimmy left the role of Adam Donovan in Hollyoaks back in May 2018, after being shot dead by his on screen father Glenn (Bob Cryer).

Opening up about his exit from the soap, Jimmy admitted that he was "really happy" with Adam's dramatic storyline.

"I think it's really, really shocking. I like the build-up to it – a good guy gone bad and then it turns back round, but then it's too late," he said.

Hollyoaks star Jimmy Essex speaks out on Adam's exit in goodbye video
=====================================================================

"I think it's really, really shocking."

By [Rianne Houghton](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/623501/rhoughton/ "Rianne Houghton")Published: 24 May 2018

![Image 4: Adam Donovan in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/21/1526998985-soaps-hollyoaks-adam-donovan-1-tjavlksex2rpvevnkupt-2.png?resize=640:*)

Lime Pictures

After all the recent twists and turns in [_Hollyoaks_](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/), you'd be forgiven for thinking that Adam Donovan might just do a Sienna Blake and return from the dead.

(Wishful thinking, we know.)

What to Read Next
-----------------

Unfortunately for us, that's not the case, as _Hollyoaks_ star Jimmy Essex has officially bid farewell to his character and the soap's cast and crew in his goodbye video.

![Image 5: youtube](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/youtube.ce3e1ae.svg?primary=currentColor&id=link-out-embed)[View full post on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/embed/qBtUj8FnIq8?start=0&enablejsapi=1&origin=https://www.digitalspy.com&autoplay=0)

Reflecting on his two-and-a-half years on the show, Jimmy thanked both the "brilliant" _Hollyoaks_ team and the fans for their support.

Opening up about his exit from 'Oaks, Jimmy admitted that he was "really happy" with Adam's dramatic exit, [where he was shot by his father Glenn](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a857795/hollyoaks-adam-death-fans-react/).

"I think it's really, really shocking. I like the build-up to it – a good guy gone bad and then it turns back round, but then it's too late," he said.

"It makes Bob's character, Glenn, so evil, doesn't it? I like that."

![Image 6: Glenn Donovan is distraught in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/21/1527003140-soaps-hollyoaks-glenn-distraught-16gpxuprk7bievhfpbdnc-1.png?resize=980:*)[![Image 7: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a857903/hollyoaks-cast-jimmy-essex-adam-donovan-exit/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/21/1527003140-soaps-hollyoaks-glenn-distraught-16gpxuprk7bievhfpbdnc-1.png?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

**Related:** [**Hollyoaks reveals Glenn Donovan fightback as Maxine agrees to help the police**](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a857828/hollyoaks-spoilers-glenn-donovan-maxine-fightback/)

Bob Cryer, who plays the sinister Glenn, is also quite fond of the Donovans' storyline, telling **Digital Spy** that it's ["great fun to play" such a baddie](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/interviews/a857475/hollyoaks-bob-cryer-depression-glenn-donovan-future/).

Hinting that fans may have to wait a while for Glenn's comeuppance, Bob said of his character's future: "I just take each day as it comes.

"But Glenn is definitely running out of friends – if he had any to begin with!"

The X-Factor Judges’ Houses Line-Up Is Revealed
===============================================

24th September 2012

10:13am BST

[Her](https://her.ie/author/her-ie)

![Image 9: The X-Factor Judges’ Houses Line-Up Is Revealed](https://her.ie/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcms.her.ie%2Fuploads%2F2012%2F09%2Fd577578cef35931deeafd7b250c690c4533d8790.jpg&w=1536&q=75)

**The auditions are over, the boot-camp has been done…  it’s getting closer to the live shows, but first, we have the much-anticipated _X-Factor_ judges’ houses.**

The 25 acts who have made it to the penultimate stage of the contest were revealed last night as the boot-camp shows came to an end.

Two groups, Times Red and Union J, who thought they had been dropped from _The X Factor_ found themselves through to the judges’ houses as Rough Copy were eliminated from the show. It was revealed a band member, Kazeem Ajobo, had a visa application that was being considered by the UK Border Agency and there were fears that if he travelled abroad he may not be able to re-enter the UK.  
  
Along with five other groups and six acts from each of the girls, boys and the older “overs” categories, they were put through to the next stage amid tears, drama and a multitude of hugs.  
  
The successful acts will be hoping to be among the three acts which each of the judges will take through to the live finals.  
  
The contestants through to judges’ houses are:  
  
**The ‘Overs’ will join Barlow at a stately home in Northamptonshire with guest mentor Cheryl Cole:**

*   Christopher Maloney, 34, a customer services adviser from Liverpool.
*   Brad Shackleton, 37, a motivational speaker from London
*   Melanie Masson, 44, a full-time mum who also runs an under-fives singing class, from Glasgow
*   Kye Sones, 30, a chimney sweep from London.
*   Carolynne Poole, 32, a casino singer and furniture restorer from Huddersfield
*   Nicola-Marie Bloor, 35, an Amy Winehouse and Lady Gaga tribute act from Derbyshire

**The ‘Boys’ will join Scherzinger at a luxury resort in Dubai with guest mentor Ne-yo**

*   Jake Quickenden, 23, a lifeguard from Scunthorpe
*   Jahmene Douglas, 21, a supermarket worker from Swindon
*   Rylan Clark, 23, a model from EssexJames Arthur, 24, a singer-songwriter from Middlesbrough
*   Adam Burridge, 23, an admin assistant from Middlesex
*   Nathan Fagan-Gayle, 25, a singer-songwriter from London
*   James Arthur, 24, a singer-songwriter from Middlesbrough

**The ‘Girls’ will join Tulisa on the island of St Lucia with guest mentor Tinie Tempah**

*   Amy Mottram, 16, a student from Essex
*   Leanne Robinson, 22, a sales assistant from London
*   Jade Collins, 17, a student from Belfast
*   Lucy Spraggan, 20, a portrait seller from Sheffield
*   Ella Henderson, 16, a student from Lincolnshire
*   Jade Ellis, 25, a bike mechanic from London

**The ‘Groups’ will join Walsh in Las Vegas with guest mentor Sharon Osbourne**

*   Poisonous Twin (Sophie, 21 and Hattie, 23) from Liverpool
*   Mitsotu (Jimmy, 23, Holly, 22, James, 22) from Harrow, north London, and Kent
*   MK1 (Simeon, Lotte) from London
*   Duke (Marko, 26, Ed, 39, Flynn, 31) from Gloucestershire
*   Union J (JJ ,23, George, 18, Josh, 19, Jaymi, 22)
*   GMD3 (Greg, 17, Dan, 19, Mickey, 17) from Windsor
*   Times Red (Staz, 20, Scott, 25, Luke, 24) from Essex

_Stay tuned in next Saturday night at 20:00 on UTV to see the X-Factor judges whittle their groups down to 12 for this year's live shows._
